transcript: Love musicals. I love Disney. So naturally, I had to see The Little Mermaid live action. And you know what? I actually really liked it. Now, for anybody that's followed me for a very, very long time, you may recall, I do not like The Little Mermaid animated. I find Ariel to be one of the more annoying princesses in the animated version. I just feel like she's so rude to her father. And then she sees Eric and she's like, Yeah, I just wanna go to the land. Which may honestly have always been the case, but I feel like in a live action version, they made it much more clear that her motivation to go to the land was to explore new worlds. And her attraction to Eric from the beginning is less, oh, here's a hot guy dancing, and much more, wow, he thinks the same way I do. Love, love, love those changes. Also, in Disney animated films, they tend to just forget that new songs were written for a Broadway show, and so they write new songs. Which, of course, is also partially because Oscars. And I really like the new songs in this movie. Wild Uncharted Waters, I think, is just as good of a song as her voice, while also driving home the theme of both of these people being kind of trapped in their circumstances. I think for the First Time is a great new song to replace, uh, Beyond My Wildest Dreams. It's not the name of the song, I just keep thinking Wildest Dreams, but that's Taylor Swift. But for the First Time is an absolutely great song. I hope this is the one they submit to the Oscars. And then of course you have the scuttlebutt, which is like Lin Manuel Miranda wrote his own version of The Morning Report from Lion King. It's not a great song, but it serves its purpose and kids seem to love it, so, you know, whatever. Halle Bailey is absolutely perfect as Ariel. I think she captured her so well. But also, in my opinion, she made Ariel likable again. I don't like Ariel in the animated version, but she made her seem so real. And it definitely felt more of a relatable relationship with a father where she just felt trapped because her father is controlling versus her just being obnoxious about her father being controlling. I don't know how to fully describe it, but it's such a small little nuance that I think made the entire story better, in my opinion. The one thing I have to criticize is y'all. The effects were awful. Now this is a movie that offers a 3 D option I saw in 2 D, and I have seen movies that looked better in 3 D than they did in their 2 D counterparts. So maybe if I go see it again I will try for the 3 D version. But there was some CGI, especially All of the faraway shots of the mermaid swimming, that were just atrocious. But it was hit or miss. There were shots underwater of just the fish and the ocean that were stunning. But I swear in the council scene in the beginning, it looked like triton's face was coming off of his head. It makes me worried that the effects in this were rushed or that they tried to be cheap on it. And by the way, if we're talking about unions, if anybody should be unionizing, is this visual effects artist. So overworked and underpaid. And I think sometimes stuff gets rushed and it leads to some not great shots. But other than that, I was pleasantly surprised. I thought this was an improvement on the animated film, and it's maybe one of my favorite live action.
